title: Demonstrations held across Turkey against violence against women
seoTitle: Istanbul protests against violence on women

tea.why: Protesters gathered to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women and denounce rising femicide rates.
tea.want: Participants demanded stronger protections for women and criticized the state's withdrawal from the Istanbul Convention.
tea.changed: Nov 25: Thousands demonstrated in multiple cities, with approximately 3,000 participants in Istanbul despite a ban on Taksim Square protests.

summary: On November 25, 2026, thousands of people participated in demonstrations across Turkey to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. In Istanbul, approximately 3,000 protesters gathered under heavy police presence after authorities prohibited a march at Taksim Square. Similar rallies occurred in Ankara, Diyarbakır, and Izmir. Organised by groups including the platform 'We Will Stop Femicide', the protests highlighted concerns over the rising number of women killed in the country. Participants criticised the government's 2021 withdrawal from the Istanbul Convention, arguing it has contributed to increased violence. President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan addressed the day by framing various forms of social and political pressure as violence, while also criticising global concepts of gender equality. Police maintained a strong presence throughout the events.
demands: Re-evaluate state policies regarding women's safety
response: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan stated that psychological pressure on women based on their beliefs, lifestyle, or clothing constitutes violence, while also criticising global gender equality concepts as a form of 'de-gendering' policy.

updates.text: Thousands participated in rallies across Turkey, including Istanbul, Ankara, and Diyarbakır, to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence.
